signature.name: Glenelg Beach
signature.detail: Adelaide's classic seaside escape, with a long sandy beach, a lively pier and a tram that runs straight from the city centre. It is the easiest place to combine a city break with a swim. Take the tram from Victoria Square; go on a warm afternoon and stay for sunset over the water.

signature.name: Adelaide Central Market
signature.detail: A buzzing indoor market in the heart of the city, packed with fresh produce, cheese, coffee and small eateries. It is the best single place to taste local South Australian food. Visit on a weekday morning when it is busy but not crammed, and bring cash for small stalls.

signature.name: Adelaide Botanic Garden
signature.detail: A large, free garden next to the city centre with glasshouses, a rose garden and shady paths. It is a peaceful must-see for anyone wanting a break from the streets. Enter from North Terrace and go early in the day to avoid the heat.

signature.name: Art Gallery of South Australia
signature.detail: One of Australia's finest art museums, with strong Australian and Indigenous collections and a grand historic facade on North Terrace. Entry is free, making it an easy must-see. Check opening hours before you go, as it closes in the evening.

signature.name: Hahndorf
signature.detail: A historic German-settled village in the Adelaide Hills, known for its main street of old buildings, bakeries and craft shops. It is a popular day trip from the city. It is easiest to reach by car or a organised tour; go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

signature.name: National Wine Centre of Australia
signature.detail: A modern wine museum and tasting venue at the edge of the Botanic Garden, introducing the wines of South Australia's regions. It is a good first stop for anyone planning to explore wine country. Book a tasting in advance and walk there from North Terrace.

signature.name: Coopers Brewery
signature.detail: Australia's largest independent family-owned brewery, a landmark for beer lovers. Tours show the brewing process and end with tastings. Tours must be booked ahead and run on set days, so check times before travelling to the site.

signature.name: Adelaide Showgrounds
signature.detail: A large events and amusement site best known for hosting the annual Royal Adelaide Show. It is worth checking what is on during your visit. It is a short tram or train ride from the city centre; buy tickets online to skip queues.

transport: Tram to Glenelg around $4; city buses and trains similar
